page: Amazon Web Services r7iz.8xlarge is a memory-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores using the x86_64 Intel Xeon 6455B processor, which operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The instance is equipped with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory running at 5 GHz, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

The server demonstrates strong performance characteristics, particularly in memory bandwidth and single-core processing. In benchmark testing, it achieves top-tier results in Geekbench single-core, image processing, and text processing tests. Large-block memory read and write operations register in the top 25% tier, supported by the high-speed DDR5 memory architecture. Additionally, the CPU features Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512), which contribute to strong performance in low-latency LLM inference tasks for small and medium models.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the r7iz.8xlarge offers a high-density memory configuration paired with high-frequency dedicated compute resources, making it a specialized option for workloads requiring both rapid CPU execution and large memory footprints. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs represents a tradeoff, focusing the hardware profile strictly on memory-bound and compute-heavy tasks. This configuration is highly suited for relational databases, in-memory caches, enterprise applications, and data processing workloads that benefit from high single-core speeds and DDR5 memory bandwidth.
